author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard launched ballistic missiles toward a U.S. military base near Azraq, Jordan, and attacked ships in the Strait of Hormuz in a new escalation reported early Wednesday.

Reuters reported that Iran said it targeted 10 vessels, including two U.S. ships. Iranian authorities claimed damage at the Jordanian base, while Jordanian and U.S. officials reported no casualties and said most incoming missiles were intercepted. Independent confirmation of Iran’s damage claims was not immediately available.

The attacks followed the U.S. military’s destruction of five Iranian oil tankers, which Washington said was retaliation for strikes on an American warship. The exchange comes as fighting also threatens energy facilities and commercial shipping around the Gulf.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global oil exports, making any attack on vessels there consequential beyond the immediate military confrontation. Details about damage to the ships and the exact sequence of the attacks remained limited in the first report. This is a developing story, and casualty or damage assessments may change as governments and shipping operators release verified updates.
dek: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard launched missiles toward a U.S. base and said it struck 10 ships after American forces destroyed five Iranian tankers.
headline: Iran attacks U.S. base in Jordan and ships near Hormuz
location: Jordan and the Strait of Hormuz
